title: Hosted schema reconciliation and migration ledger
goal: Make staging schema, production migration history, generated types, and the launch migration ledger agree without destructive resets

in: Active Supabase migration chain and hosted staging/production migration history
Launch-required classification, one-at-a-time evidence, advisors, type generation, and forward repair
out: Destructive reset, forced replay, or automatic production migration application

Launch-required migrations have one-at-a-time staging evidence, advisor output, and forward-repair instructions

wave34.headline: The Wave 33 launch blocker is WITHDRAWN. The generated contract IS reproducible from the active chain: 0 contract columns, 0 relations and 0 callables lack chain provenance. The chain is a strict SUPERSET, so a regeneration can only add coverage.
wave34.retracted: Wave 33 reported public.venue_profiles as 42 contract columns vs 19 chain columns, and generalised that to 130 out-of-band columns across 23 relations, on the strength of supabase/tests/db008_chain_column_replay.mjs. That script had four defects, all inflating apparent drift: case-sensitive `add column` matching inside matchAll() (so every upper-case-DDL migration contributed zero columns), `add constraint` recorded as a column named `constraint`, `alter table if exists` before a relation CREATE treated as having created it, and DROP/CREATE applied in per-kind loop order so `drop view; create view` in one migration inverted. The 42-vs-19 figure and the 130-column figure are both artefacts and are withdrawn.

instrumentCorrected: supabase/tests/db008_chain_contract_replay.mjs - new, replaces db008_chain_column_replay.mjs. Case-insensitive, single ordered event stream with byte offsets, existence-guard modelling (`alter table if exists` and to_regclass-guarded ALTERs are modelled as no-ops), constraint keywords excluded from the column set, RENAME COLUMN handled, an audited dynamic-DDL supplement for the one `execute format` loop, and per-surface reproducibility reporting (table columns, relations, callables, view columns).

supabase/tests/db008_contract_reproducibility.harness.sh - new. 33 checks: 13 instrument self-assertions (positive controls on each defect class), 5 negative controls, 6 post-state re-assertions, and a cross-implementation agreement check against the Wave 33 surface replay.

supabase/tests/db008_contract_attribution_audit.mjs - new. Independently re-reads the cited migration for every one of 5170 contract columns and requires it to mention both the relation and the column.

supabase/tests/db008_chain_surface_replay.mjs - two Wave 33 counting defects fixed: contract callables 125 -> 100 (it counted only functions with a literal `Args: {` block and so missed every zero-argument callable), and its output now agrees with the new replay on the relation count (415).

supabase/tests/db008_storage_replay_guard.harness.sh - the Wave 33 harness reported `replay-safety: 0 passed, 0 failed` and EXITED 0 because its scenario manifest and 00-bootstrap fixture were never committed, so it iterated zero times. Zero scenarios is now a hard failure with the missing prerequisites named. It currently exits 1 with those names; the fixture still has to be committed or regenerated.
wave34.negativeControlDefectFoundInMyOwnHarness: The first revision of the reproducibility harness built all five negative controls by REMOVING contract surface. A superset check can only be broken by an ADDITION, so all five passed against a gate that could not fail. The controls are now additions (extra column, extra relation, extra callable, extra view column) plus a fifth that asserts a removal is TOLERATED, so an over-strict gate is caught too. Same lesson class as the Wave 33 note about a harness that passed 7/7 while its emulation had silently failed to rebuild.
residualHonestGaps: 13 view relations are proven by column-name occurrence in their defining migration, not by replaying the SELECT list. All 13 currently have 0 columns without an occurrence and a negative control pins that half of the gate, but it is the one surface where a regeneration could still remove coverage.

Six ALTERs are skipped by a fresh replay because version order is not calendar order (20250904110000 runs before 20260413200000). All six are guarded, so none is a chain abort. Five are harmless because the later CREATE supplies the columns. ONE is a genuine live-versus-fresh divergence: scheduled_posts.platform_status / platform_errors. The contract does not declare them either, so the two agree today; if any live target has them, regeneration would drop them. Routed as HF-DB-011-SCHEDULED-POSTS-FRESH-CHAIN-DIVERGENCE.
